FOREWORD 



This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 27 April 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Small Tools Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical 
Engineering Division Council. 

This standard has been prepared based on the prevalent practices in Indian industry and develop- 
ments at international level. In the preparation of this standard, considerable assistance has been 
derived from: 



DIN 8377 : 1981 



Subland twist drills with morse taper shank for clearance holes and counter- 
bores for hexagon socket head cap screws and slotted cheese head screws 
Deutsches Institut fur Normung ( DIN ). 

The other Indian Standards in this series are: 

IS 12687 : 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with morse taper shank for countersunk 
holes prior to tapping screw threads — Specification 

IS 12688: 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with morse taper shank for clearance 
holes and countersinks for countersunk head screws prior to tapping screw 
threads — Specification 

IS 12689 : 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with morse taper shank for clearance 
holes and counterbores for slotted cheese head screws— Specification 

IS 12691:1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with parallel shank for holes prior to 
tapping screw threads — Specification 

IS 12692 : 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills^ with parallel shank for clearance holes 
and countersinks for countersunk liead screws — Specification

IS 12690 : 1989 



Indian Standard 

SMALL TOOLS — SUBLAND TWIST DRILLS 

WITH MORSE TAPER SHANK FOR 

CLEARANCE HOLES AND COUNTERBORES 

FOR SLOTTED CHEESE HEAD 

SCREWS — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers dimensions and other 
requirements lor the subland twist drills with 
morse taper shanks for producing clearance holes 
and counlerbores lor slotted cheese head screws 
of M5 to M20 — Medium series conforming to 
IS 3406 ( Part 2 ) : 1986 'Dimensions for counter- 
sinks and counterbores : Part 2 Counterborcs 
( second revision )\ 

2 REFERENCES 

IS No. Title 

IS 1715 : 1986 Dimensions for self holding 
tapers ( second revision ) 

IS 3406 Dimensions for counterbores : 

( Part 2 ; :I1986 Part 2 Counterbores ( second 
levision ) 

Technical supply conditions 
for twist drills (^rjr revi- 
sion ) 



IS 5099 : 1983 



IS 7778 : 1975 
IS 10915: 1984 



Methods for sampling small 
tools 

Terms, definitions and types 
of twist drills 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.1 For the purpose of this standard the defini- 
tions given in IS 10915 : 1984 shall apply. 

4 DIMENSIONS 

4.1 Dimensions of subland twist drills shall be as 
given Table 1 . 

4.2 Tolerance 

The tolerance on flute length /j and overall 
length / shall be ±5 mm. 

5 MATERIAL 

5*1 The material of subland twist drill shall be 
as gi\cn in IS 5099 : 1983. 

6 HARDNESS 

6*1 The hardness of subland twist drill shall be 
as given in IS 5099 : 1983. 

7 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

7.1 Tool Type *N\ right hand cutting will be 



supplied unless otherwise specified. 

7.2 The diameter ^ and rf, shall be measured as 
near to the point as practicable. 

7.3 While using this drill, cutting speed should 
be selected according to the large diameter V* 
and the feed rate according to small ( pilot ) 
diameter *d{, 

7.4 For the requirements not covered in this 
standard, the twist drill shall conform to the 
requirements as given in IS 5099 : 1983. 

8 PROTECTIVE COATING 

8.1 Protective coating on subland twist drill shall 
be as given in IS 5099 : 1983. 

9 SAMPLING 

9.1 The sampling and criteria of acceptance shall 
be in accordance with IS 7778 : 1975. 

10 TESTS 

10.1 Subland twist drills shall be tested as eiven 
in IS 5099 : 1983. 

11 DESIGNATION 

11.1 A subland twist drill with morse tarer 
shank, having diameter d ^-= 18 mm and step 
diameter rfj = 110 mm Tool Type N, for right 
hand cutting made of high speed steel and 
conforming to this standard shall be designated 
as: 

Subland Twist Drill 18 x 1 1 — IS 12690 

11.2 When required with tool type other than 
'N\ *H' or *S' should be added in the designation 
after the diameter as appropriate. 

12 MARKING 

12.1 Subland twist drills shall be marked as 
given in IS 5099: 1983. 

13 PACKING AND PACKAGING 

13.1 Subland twist drills shall be packed as given 
in IS 5099 : 1983.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureao of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harhionious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of 
goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copfrright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use» in 
the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or 
urade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

f

are issued from, time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession 
of the latest amendments or edition Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent to BIS giving
